corrections.source_says: Add the separate post-study model-only ablation of associative versus non-associative prompting. GPT-5 was queried using the 24 initial HAICo prompts, three times per condition with 9 ideas per run; CLIP ViT-bigG-14 pairwise cosine distances were averaged across runs. Associative prompting produced greater idea diversity (W = 24.0, p < 0.001). These are 24 prompt-level input cases, not an additional randomized human sample; classify this study model_only, question none, and leave human-participant counts null. Numerical arm means and SDs are not printed.

confirmed: The document is the 35-page preprint arXiv:2512.18388v2 [cs.HC], stamped 6 Apr 2026; the recorded title and author list match (p. 1; PDF page count). The entire markdown conversion, including Appendices A-D, was read.

Randomized people study confirmed: two participants were randomly assigned to each of 12 sequences varying task pairing, task order and HAICo/ChatGPT order; all 24 people used both systems. Both arm counts refer to the same people (pp. 8-9, Section 5; p. 31, Table 5).

lab_rct and context_class none are appropriate: this is a supervised laboratory comparison of AI configurations with creativity scored on participant-produced posters (p. 26, Appendix C.1, Study Environment; p. 10, Section 5.3).

The 24 participants contributed to the main poster evaluation; diversity excluded three people who downloaded only one image for both systems, leaving N = 21. Both analysis counts are below the codebook threshold of 50 people, so core no is correct (p. 27, Appendix C.3; p. 10, Section 5.3).
The output corpus contained 123 posters: 63 ChatGPT and 60 HAICo; these are image counts, separate from the 24 people (p. 27, Appendix C.3).

Demographics match the form: 10 female, 13 male and 1 non-binary; ages 24-34, M = 28.2, SD = 2.8; 21 of 24 were from computer science/information technology. Recruitment was from a local technology-focused university, and compensation was a EUR 20 voucher plus a reusable bag; the study country is not explicitly named (p. 9, Section 5.1).

The task used two creation sessions within the study: 20 minutes of co-creation in each 40-minute session, with an overall duration of about 1 hour 50 minutes. The three poster topics in the form match the instructions (pp. 8-9, Sections 5-5.2 and Fig. 4; p. 30, Fig. 12).

Both systems used GPT-5 for text and matched final-image models: gpt-image-1, then gpt-image-1.5. Each image-model version was used by 12 participants; Appendix A.2 also identifies gpt-image-1-mini for HAICo thumbnails (p. 8, Section 5 and footnote 1; p. 23, Appendix A.2).

Novelty and usefulness used five non-author raters on 5-point scales; four raters had participated in the study. They were blind to generating system and participant identity; scores were averaged over raters, images within participant-system pairs, then participants. ICC(2,5) = 0.61 for novelty and 0.60 for usefulness (p. 10, Section 5.3; pp. 27-28, Appendix C.3).
S1-O1.reported is exact: HAICo novelty M = 3.22 versus ChatGPT M = 2.41; W = 0.0, p < 0.001. Statistical comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (p. 11, Fig. 5c caption; p. 9, Section 5.3).

S1-O2.reported is exact: HAICo image-set diversity M = 0.48 versus ChatGPT M = 0.36; W = 26.0, p = 0.001, with N = 21. It is average pairwise cosine distance between CLIP ViT-bigG-14 image embeddings within each person and system, so flexibility/with_ai is appropriate rather than across_people (p. 10, Section 5.3; p. 11, Fig. 5c caption).

S1-O3.reported and the one-line finding correctly state that fluency and usefulness did not differ significantly; Fig. 5c provides plotted results without numerical means or test statistics for these two outcomes. The numbers in the one-line finding match the PDF (p. 11, Fig. 5c and caption; p. 10 for diversity N = 21).
This is not a synthesis, so the default null synthesis counts and empty pooled estimates are appropriate (pp. 8-12, Sections 5-6.2).
summary: The paper contains a randomized within-person laboratory comparison of HAICo and ChatGPT with 24 people (21 for image-set diversity), requiring two-screener review but falling below the 50-person core threshold. The source version and main reported results are correct; six corrections address omitted outcomes and a model-only ablation, included appendices, company affiliations, and unsupported student status.
